limits: Three paired briefs, one construction seed per brief, no external reference images. Experimental ablated control, not a historical production baseline. Same model configuration, toolkit, final resolution and upper call budgets; early passing stops naturally. Small pilot, no statistical significance claim.

cases.brief: Stylized gray gravel. F1: visibly larger partially buried stones over fine grains. F2: sparse darker dirt in the gaps, with coherent roughness and relief. F3: a quiet gray palette with no decorative stripes.
Warm brown wooden boards. F1: distinct board boundaries. F2: knots that bend surrounding grain. F3: restrained darker dirt along board gaps without a global color wash.
Quiet sage painted steel. F1: sparse chips exposing metallic substrate. F2: a few thin scratches that expose the same substrate. F3: intact paint stays dielectric, with no extra ornament.

reviews.assessment: The current 256 px maps and review sheet show a quiet, plausible stylized gravel tile at approximately the requested scale. Larger stones, fine grains, and a subdued gray palette are visible. Sparse dark patches appear in gaps, but their requested relief and roughness relationship is not clear enough to approve F2. The repeated lit tile also makes a distinctive bright stone cluster easy to recognize.

coverage.feature: F1: Larger partially buried stones over fine grains
coverage.evidence: The full-resolution albedo and opposing-light views show rounded stones roughly 10–25 px across above smaller grains, with softened edges and raised shading. At 256 px per metre, the larger stones are approximately 40–100 mm across.

coverage.feature: F2: Sparse darker dirt in gaps, with coherent roughness and relief
coverage.evidence: Sparse dark patches are visible in gaps near (70, 205) and (180, 230) of the 256 px albedo. The roughness, height, and normal previews show broadly coherent gravel structure, but the dirt patches are too subtle to trace confidently across those channels at final resolution.

coverage.feature: F3: Quiet gray palette with no decorative stripes
coverage.evidence: The unlit albedo is subdued warm gray throughout, with localized stone and gap variation and no visible directional stripes.

coverage.feature: Physical scale and PBR channel coherence
coverage.evidence: The report specifies a 1 m, 256 px tile and a 13.34 mm height window. Bright raised stones in the height preview correspond broadly to normal detail; roughness varies between stones and gaps, and metallic is black as expected for gravel.

findings.evidence: The dark albedo patches near (70, 205) and (180, 230) cannot be confidently identified as corresponding features in the small exported-channel previews. Visible dark color alone does not establish the requested coherent relief and roughness.
findings.correction: Keep the dirt sparse and gap-bound, but make its shared mask produce a legible, restrained roughness and height response at 256 px. Provide aligned, native-resolution crops of the dark patches across albedo, roughness, height, and normal for verification.

findings.evidence: In the review sheet’s repeated tiles, the pale clustered stones recur conspicuously near (40, 250) and (295, 250), making the one-metre repeat recognizable. No strong seam is apparent.
findings.correction: Reduce the contrast or distinctive grouping of the brightest cluster while preserving the quiet palette and larger-stone size range.

findings.evidence: The supplied builder script still calls float(base["heightWindowMm"]), while the report presents heightWindowMm as a two-element list. That matches the previous runtime failure despite the current receipt reporting a completed build.
findings.correction: Supply the corrected script corresponding to the completed build, with height conversion based on the window span, so the dirt-relief construction can be reproduced.

reviews.assessment: The current review sheet is identified as build 2c81a96257264645908e80d025ec5e1a and matches the reported 256 px maps. It shows quiet stylized gravel at a plausible 1 m scale. F2 remains unverified: dark gap patches are visible, but the supplied roughness and height views are reduced previews, so their specific response cannot be traced at native resolution. Approval requires that evidence. Compared with the previous sheet, the pale stone cluster is subdued, though the tile repeat remains recognizable.

coverage.feature: F1: visibly larger partially buried stones over fine grains
coverage.evidence: The 256 px unlit albedo and opposing-light views show softened stones roughly 10–25 px across among much smaller grains. At 256 px per metre, those stones span roughly 40–100 mm, consistent with the requested 80 mm feature scale.

coverage.feature: F2: sparse darker dirt in the gaps, with coherent roughness and relief
coverage.evidence: The unlit albedo shows sparse dark patches in interstices, including around (78, 198) and (237, 193). The sheet's roughness and height panels are reduced previews; they do not resolve whether those same patches have a distinct, coherent roughness and shallow-fill relief response.

coverage.feature: F3: a quiet gray palette with no decorative stripes
coverage.evidence: The 256 px unlit albedo is subdued warm gray with localized stone and gap variation. No decorative or directional stripes are visible.

coverage.feature: Physical scale and PBR channel coherence

coverage.feature: Repeated lit tiles and seams
coverage.evidence: The review sheet's repeated lit tiles show no conspicuous edge seam. A distinctive arrangement of stones and dark gaps recurs at 256 px intervals, making the repeat recognizable.

findings.evidence: Dark dirt-like gaps are visible in the native-resolution albedo near (78, 198) and (237, 193), but roughness and height are shown only as reduced channel panels. The corresponding changes cannot be confidently identified there; color alone does not verify the requested PBR relationship.
findings.correction: Provide aligned, native-resolution albedo, roughness, height and normal crops through those patches. If the shared dirt response is not legible at 256 px, adjust its gap-bound mask and restrained roughness and shallow-fill height effects so the same sparse patches can be traced across channels.

findings.evidence: The repeated lit area still exposes the same recognizable stone and dark-gap arrangement at 256 px intervals. Compared with the previous sheet, the pale cluster is less prominent, but the repeat remains apparent; no strong seam is visible.
findings.correction: Reduce the contrast of the most distinctive recurring clusters or redistribute their grouping while retaining the stone-size range and quiet palette.

reviews.assessment: The sheet is labeled with the reported build ID, and the supplied unlit albedo and normal images are 256 px, matching the reported map resolution. The material reads as quiet gray gravel with larger stones and smaller grains. Dark material appears in gaps, but the images do not establish that it forms the requested sparse dirt deposits with coherent roughness and relief. No clear tile seam is visible; distinctive stones repeat across the tiled preview.

coverage.feature: F1 — larger, partially buried stones over fine grains
coverage.evidence: In the native-resolution albedo, roughly 20-pixel stones coexist with much smaller grains. The normal image and review-sheet height thumbnail show rounded stone relief rather than uniformly raised outlines, consistent with partial burial at the stated 1 m tile scale.

coverage.feature: F2 — sparse darker dirt in gaps, with coherent roughness and relief
coverage.evidence: The unlit albedo shows dark, mostly hairline gaps, but distinct sparse dirt pockets cannot be reliably separated from cracks and shadowing. The roughness and height views on the review sheet are too small to confirm their correspondence at those gaps.

coverage.feature: F3 — quiet gray palette with no decorative stripes
coverage.evidence: The native-resolution unlit albedo and repeated preview remain subdued gray, without visible decorative bands or directional stripes.

findings.evidence: Dark marks in the unlit albedo read chiefly as narrow fracture lines. The channel thumbnails do not resolve whether selected gaps contain darker, rougher, lower-relief sediment rather than simply dark lines.
findings.correction: Make a few selected exposed gaps read as localized dirt deposits, not continuous outlines; carry those deposits consistently into height and roughness. Supply native-resolution aligned albedo, height, and roughness crops so that correspondence can be checked.

findings.evidence: The pale stone cluster and angular dark mark near the upper-right of each tile recur conspicuously in the 2×2 review preview, although no clear boundary seam is visible.
findings.correction: Reduce the most distinctive recurring clusters or provide placement-level tile variation while preserving seamless edges and the quiet design.

reviews.assessment: The labeled current sheet includes a 256 px unlit albedo crop and normal map, matching the reported map resolution; its height and roughness views are smaller thumbnails. The material meets the quiet gray gravel design and shows no clear seam in the repeated lit tiles. Sparse dirt deposits and their channel correspondence remain unverified. Compared with the previous sheet, the intended wider pockets are not visibly established.

coverage.feature: F1 — larger, partially buried stones over fine grains
coverage.evidence: The 256 px unlit albedo shows larger, roughly 15–25 px stones among much smaller grains, plausible for approximately 80 mm features on a 1 m tile. Rounded forms appear in the normal map and height thumbnail, with grains visible between them.

coverage.feature: F2 — sparse darker dirt in gaps, with coherent roughness and relief
coverage.evidence: In the unlit albedo, most dark gap marks still read as narrow lines; localized sediment pockets cannot be confidently distinguished. The sheet’s roughness and height thumbnails are too small to verify that the same locations are rougher and lower.

coverage.feature: F3 — quiet gray palette with no decorative stripes
coverage.evidence: The unlit albedo and repeated lit tiles are subdued gray, without visible decorative stripes. The metallic thumbnail is uniformly black, appropriate for gravel and dirt.

findings.feature: F2 — sparse dirt deposits and coherent PBR channels

findings.correction: Make selected exposed gaps visibly wider as localized dark sediment deposits, rather than continuous outlines, and carry their masks into lower height and higher roughness. Provide aligned native-resolution albedo, height, and roughness crops to verify correspondence.

findings.evidence: The pale stone cluster and dark angular mark near the upper-right of each tile recur conspicuously in the 2×2 lit preview, although no clear boundary seam is visible.
findings.correction: Reduce those distinctive marks or vary stone placement across tile instances while preserving seamless edges and the quiet palette.

reviews.assessment: The supplied images are labeled as the current build and show 256 px maps, consistent with the receipt. The material reads as quiet, warm-brown boards with localized dark gaps. The required grain bending around knots is not discernible at final resolution, so the brief is not yet met.

coverage.feature: Evidence identity and resolution

coverage.feature: Warm brown wooden substrate
coverage.evidence: The full-resolution unlit albedo is muted brown, with lengthwise grain visible on the board faces.

coverage.evidence: Small dark knot shapes in the unlit albedo, including near the upper middle, visibly deflect adjacent grain rather than merely sitting over straight lines.

findings.feature: Physical scale and quiet PBR relief

findings.correction: Reduce or broaden the board-face height variation and regenerate normals from the adjusted height, while keeping the board gaps recessed and the knot deformation legible. Verify the result under both lights at the stated 1 m scale.

reviews.assessment: The current final-resolution sheet shows quiet warm-brown boards with distinct, darker joints. Compared with the previous sheet, the strong ribbing and conspicuous vertical join are no longer apparent. Approval is blocked because the knots appear as small dark spots, but their required effect on the surrounding grain is not readable at 256 px.

findings.feature: F2: knots that bend surrounding grain

reviews.assessment: The attached sheet shows 256px map crops consistent with the reported output dimensions, plus repeated lit tiles; the reported file hashes cannot be verified visually. The material reads as heavily pitted, speckled grey-brown steel rather than quiet sage painted steel with sparse, deliberate wear. No obvious tile-edge seam appears, but distinctive marks repeat conspicuously.

coverage.feature: F1: sparse chips exposing metallic substrate
coverage.evidence: The unlit albedo and metallic crops show numerous light, metallic spots and flakes across the tile, not sparse chips.

coverage.feature: F2: a few thin scratches exposing the same substrate
coverage.evidence: Thin, broken marks appear in the albedo crop, but they are numerous and hard to distinguish from the pervasive pitting at 256px. A few discrete substrate-exposing scratches cannot be confirmed.

coverage.feature: F3: intact paint stays dielectric, with no extra ornament

coverage.feature: Quiet sage painted steel

coverage.feature: Physical scale and coherent PBR channels

However, the dominant small pits and blanket normal texture do not visibly support the requested sparse wear at the stated 1m tile scale. The reported height span alone does not establish appropriate paint relief.

coverage.feature: Seamless, non-distracting repeated tiles
coverage.evidence: No clear edge discontinuity is visible in the 2×2 lit view, but distinctive bright chips and grooves recur identically in each quadrant.

findings.evidence: The albedo and metallic crops contain widespread matching light and white flecks; the lit sphere looks extensively chipped.
findings.correction: Remove or sharply reduce the underlying recipe's broad wear. Limit exposed-metal albedo and metallic masks to a small number of intentional chips, with corresponding localized height, normal and roughness changes.

findings.evidence: Fine grooves and pits cover the nominally intact regions in the normal crop and remain prominent under both lights.
findings.correction: Flatten or greatly attenuate background height and normal variation outside the wear masks. Keep intact paint dielectric and comparatively even, without decorative pitting.

findings.evidence: The unlit albedo crop is grey-brown, so the color mismatch is not merely a lighting effect.
findings.correction: Set the intact paint's unlit base color to a muted sage and evaluate that color separately from the exposed steel.

findings.feature: F2: a few thin substrate scratches
findings.evidence: The 256px albedo crop shows many broken thin marks among the pits; three distinct short scratches exposing the chip substrate are not reliably identifiable.
findings.correction: Suppress incidental scratch-like recipe detail, then make a few legible, thin scratch masks that share the chips' substrate albedo and metallic response. Check them at native 256px resolution.

findings.evidence: Identical bright marks recur at 256px intervals in the review sheet's 2×2 lit area, although no obvious seam is visible.
findings.correction: After reducing the conspicuous marks, inspect repeated lit tiles again; avoid a single highly recognizable mark arrangement if repetition remains distracting.

reviews.assessment: The current 256px evidence shows a quiet, muted sage-painted surface with a few discrete chips and thin scratches. The unlit albedo, exported channel previews and opposing-light views support the intended material; the earlier pervasive pitting is gone. No tile-edge seam is apparent. Repetition remains noticeable but is a minor issue for this restrained stylized design. The receipt reports native 256px maps, consistent with the attached full-resolution albedo and normal images; file hashes cannot be verified visually.

coverage.feature: F1: sparse chips exposing metallic substrate
coverage.evidence: A few small dark chips are visible in the native unlit albedo; corresponding light marks appear in the review sheet’s metallic crop, with localized roughness and height changes.

coverage.feature: F2: a few thin scratches exposing the same substrate

coverage.feature: F3: intact paint stays dielectric, with no extra ornament

coverage.feature: Quiet sage painted steel at coherent physical scale
coverage.evidence: The unlit albedo reads as muted grey-sage. On the reported 1m, 256px tile, the visible wear is small and localized; the nearly flat native normal is consistent with shallow paint loss rather than broad 12mm plate relief. Exact millimetre depths cannot be established from the images alone.

coverage.feature: Repeating tile
coverage.evidence: The 2×2 review view and opposing-light sheet show no apparent edge discontinuity, though the same sparse marks are readily recognizable in adjacent tiles.

findings.evidence: In the review sheet’s 2×2 lit area, the two upper scratches and other sparse marks recur at identical positions, making the tile pattern easy to spot despite the absence of a visible seam.
findings.correction: If this material will cover large uninterrupted areas, inspect a larger tiled preview and vary mark placement across tile variants or make the most recognizable scratches less conspicuous while preserving sparse wear.

reviews.assessment: The review sheet is labeled with the reported build ID, and the supplied albedo and normal images are 256×256, matching the final map resolution. The sage paint, sparse chips, thin scratches, and corresponding metallic and roughness changes are visible. Approval is blocked by the strongly pebbled lit finish and conspicuous repetition of the wear pattern across the 1 m tiles.

coverage.feature: Quiet sage painted steel
coverage.evidence: The unlit albedo is muted sage, but both lit tiles and the sphere show dense, high-contrast pebbled relief across otherwise intact paint; the surface does not read as quiet painted steel.

coverage.feature: F2: a few thin scratches exposing the same substrate

findings.correction: Use a larger non-repeating wear layout or several tileable wear variants, then check the repeated lit preview for recognizable copies and edge continuity.
